screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows an AC source connected to one electromagnetic component — a resistor, inductor, or capacitor — and its voltage and current phasors.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a component and explore how its phasor relates to the AC drive.

intro.currentDetails: The Intro screen is in its initial state.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a series RLC circuit driven by an AC source, with resistor, inductor, and capacitor phasors.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Adjust R, L, and C to see how the series impedance phasor changes.

seriesRlc.currentDetails: The Series RLC screen is in its initial state.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the series RLC circuit swept across driving frequency, with the phase triangle alongside impedance-versus-frequency and current-versus-frequency curves.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Sweep the driving frequency to find resonance, where the reactances cancel and the phase angle goes to zero.

resonance.currentDetails: The Resonance screen is in its initial state.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the instantaneous power over a cycle, with the average real power and the oscillating reactive component shaded separately and a power-factor readout.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a Reset All button that returns the simulation to its starting state.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Adjust the load to see how the power factor changes and how a reactive load delivers zero net energy.

power.currentDetails: The Power screen is in its initial state.
